title: A sharp lower bound for some reciprocal Rado numbers
summary: Let $f_r(k)$ be the smallest $n$ such that every $r$-coloring of $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ has a monochromatic solution to the equation \[\frac{1}{x_1}+\frac{1}{x_2}+\cdots+\frac{1}{x_k}=\frac{1}{x_{k+1}}, \] where $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_k$ are not necessarily distinct. In this paper, we prove that $f_r(2)\geq 4^r/2$ for all $r\geq1$, and $f_r(k)\geq(2^r-1)k^r$ for all $k\geq3$ and $r\geq1$. When $r=2$, we show that, if $k=3\cdot2^m$ for some positive integer $m$, then $f_2(k)=3k^2$; and if $k=p^m$ for some odd prime number $p$ and positive integer $m$, then $f_2(k)\geq3k^2+1$.
